result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep corners square, allow only one stated circular exception, and build depth from hard unblurred offsets. B is more concrete: it defines rule thicknesses and a rule colour, includes a ready-to-paste prefers-reduced-motion block, and adds an accessible focus ring. A has three easing curves, which goes against the brand's near-zero motion, and it only describes reduced-motion handling instead of providing code. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both keep radius at zero with a justified circle exception, and both build depth from hard, unblurred offsets. A is stronger: it adds explicit rule-thickness tokens, separates raised elements (cards, menus) from overlays (popovers, modals), and puts the reduced-motion override in ready-to-paste CSS. B adds enter and exit easing curves that this brand doesn't need, gives no rule-thickness tokens, and only describes reduced-motion handling without the code for it.
